narration.say: This week, Google signed to buy power from its maker.
Why burn rock instead of drilling?
Every kilometer down adds about 25 degrees, enough to wreck drill bits.
But super-hot water carries far more energy.
So a fusion-style beam vaporizes rock, and gas blows it out.
The catch: the first wells will still use ordinary drills.
If beams scale, Earth's heat could run data centers day and night.
Follow Media Diet for the physics behind the headlines.

shots.beat: first frame / hook: crust cutaway, a glowing beam boring down from a rig + "This drill / has no bit."
the news: surface view — geothermal plant powers a data center through a new power line; deal chip
the question: an ordinary tri-cone bit grinding beside the beam
heat with depth: camera descends the strata, the thermometer climbs, the bit glows and breaks
super-hot water: drops go down blue and come back glowing gold
mechanism: the beam vaporizes rock at the bottom; purge gas carries it out
the limitation: the Oregon well site by a paper volcano, an ordinary rig and bit
payoff: day turns to night, the plant keeps powering the data center
CTA: Media Diet sign, a small derrick behind it
